author: veceraj
body:
This PR adds native HMAC authentication support for Google Cloud Storage (GCS) by introducing a dual-client approach. Previously, after migrating to the native GCS library (cloud.google.com/go/storage), HMAC keys stopped working because the library uses the JSON API, which does not support HMAC authentication (available only via the XML API). To restore HMAC compatibility, a new lightweight client was implemented using the MinIO SDK, which signs requests properly against GCS's S3-compatible XML API.

When users configure GCS storage, the system now automatically selects the appropriate client based on the credentials: service account JSON credentials will use the native GCS client (resumable uploads), while HMAC credentials will use the MinIO client (chunked/multipart uploads). Upload logic across S3, GCS (JSON), and GCS (HMAC) backends was unified with a new part-size computation helper, ensuring consistent multipart behavior under large files and service limits. Functionally, backup and restore workflows now behave the same for both credential types, requiring minimal or no migration effort for users upgrading from earlier PBM versions that accessed GCS via S3.

Starting in Gradle 9.0, the daemon will no longer support running on Java < 17. As such, our test infrastructure will no longer run our test suites on Java < 17.

Gradle executes across many different processes. Clients, the daemon, workers of different types, javaexec processes, etc. For the most part, our test suites implicitly use the same java version for these processes as the test suites are started with.

This commit aims to clean up existing tests that do explicitly test across java versions, and also aims to add test coverage where explicit java versions should be tested against.

This commit:

- Adds entries to SupportedJavaVersions to track the minimum wrapper and worker versions, in addition to the existing client and daemon minimum versions

- Improves test coverage for code executed in worker processes. Including:
    - PMD
    - Java compilation
    - Test execution
    - Scala compilation
    - Worker API

- Improves test coverage for code executed directly in separate java processes
    - JavaExec, ExecOperations.javaexec, ProviderFactory.javaexec
    - Javadoc tasks

- Updates tests to use more fixtures from JavaToolchainFixture

- Adds fixtures to AvailableJavaHomes to make it more easy to write tests that cover java versions that run on different Gradle processes -- client, worker, daemon

## About The Pull Request
This PR Overhauls farming. Reorganizes the mining map, and tweaks the vanguard fort; as well as relocates the soilsons and butcher closer to town.
### Farming Changes: 
The majority of the world now has 'weak' dirt. When tilled, it becomes 'poor' soil with a bad quality var for farming. Similarly, there is now 'great' dirt, which becomes great soil, and regular current dirt that becomes current soil.
Soil quality directly affects chance to get extra harvest, chance to ruin crops, and chance to ruin crops a little. 
The three soil types also have differant maximums for water, and nutrition. Poor soil holds half the water and nutrition of standard, standard soil is the(current), Feracious soil has 1.5 times the maximum amount of water and nutrition than normal soil.

By default, tilling grass with grant poor dirt. Soilsons start with great dirt in their farming areas, as well as great soil in a few spots.
The Towner farmer homes have 'average' soil within their fenced area, as does the physician.
If grass is ploughed with a plough (large dragging object) It will instead yield standard dirt.

Standard dirt and great dirt will be craftable with level 3 farming required for standard soil, and level 5 farming required for great soil.

Seeds can no longer be used to create 'soil' plots by themselves at 0 farming skill. This can be done at farming skill 2, however.

Bashing open produce/plants for seeds is now skill based instead of random; with a significant bonus provided for using a thresher to get seeds.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Mining Changes:
A second mine has been created to the east in the cave system near the water lake.
The former western mine has been moved a bit more west, and now features a levelbelow. The West mine now specifically has copper and tin, and no iron and coal.
Similarly the new Eastern mine has iron and coal, but no copper and tin.
In the same manner, the lavafissure-bog mine has recieved a significant boost in that it functions like the eastern mine but has higher drop rates for valuable ore, as well as more likely to hold ore in the first place. 
Cinnabar now only comes from the lava fissure in the bog.

Bandits can no longer get ore from mining.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Map Tweaks and Changes:
Edit 5/27: This PR has been merged with a seperate map PR moving around things in lowtown and approved by a maptainer. I'm not 100% sure on all the changes involved in it, though it primarily tweaks the mine to the west and adjusts the vanguard fort.

The soilsons has been relocated in between the lowtown and hightown. Hopefully this will provide a bit more foottraffic, leaving them less isolated in the middle of nowhere.
The primary mine has been moved more westward (filled primarily with copper and tin)
A new eastern mine has been made filled primarily with iron and coal.
Dirt everywhere on the map has been replaced with 'poor' dirt.
The vanguard fort has been made more secure; Windows in the dungeon facing outside are gone, the southern rooftop now has a murderhole wall; the northern roof with training area now has palisades.
Re-adds wolves to gem cave.

## Why It's Good For The Game
This should hopefully reduce the ease at which people who aren't farmers are farming things and flooding the in game economy with food; while making the soilsons stand out compared to druids and towner farmers.

The changes to mining should hopefully be a QOL matter for miners so they can actually /pick/ what sort of resources they're trying to get instead of having to hope they get the correct one. For that matter, since we buffed the lava mine in the bog to make it more valuable, bandits can no longer get ore from mining- something that probably should've been done ages ago.


The vanguard fort has been pathetically insecure and somewhat useless. Hopefully with the adjustments I've made it can see a bit more use in being more secure; and acting as a strong point in the lowtown.

#### What problem is this solving?

This PR introduces a feature that dynamically hides or shows the `tax` column in the VTEX Styleguide `Table` component based on the presence of tax data in the order items.
When none of the items contain tax information, the `tax` column is omitted from the schema. When at least one item has tax, the column appears automatically.

This pull request refactors the Bazel build configuration and the Rust codebase for better modularity, maintainability, and platform-specific functionality. Key changes include restructuring the Bazel build files, renaming and reorganizing Rust modules, and introducing a new example for Raspberry Pi hardware. Additionally, test scripts and configurations were updated to support these changes.

### Bazel Configuration Changes:
* Removed the `BUILD.bazel` file from the root and migrated its contents to `src/rust/BUILD.bazel` for better organization. This includes the `platform_transition_binary` rules and test configurations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7fc57714ef13c3325ce2a1130202edced92fcccc0c6db34a72f7b57f60d552a3L1-L118) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e578dc17813594117808ac73f409aa9d7f710091b399186c421f9ce3e8590d74R2-R23)
* Updated target names and dependencies in `src/rust/BUILD.bazel`, such as renaming `hello_world_host` to `basic_example_host` and replacing external crate dependencies with a `robotics_lib` library. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e578dc17813594117808ac73f409aa9d7f710091b399186c421f9ce3e8590d74R35-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e578dc17813594117808ac73f409aa9d7f710091b399186c421f9ce3e8590d74L98-R173)

### Rust Codebase Updates:

body:
1. Refactored the Solana clock thread safe wrapper by separating clock data from the clock update process. Added the new solana clock refresh period parameter to the config toml file : `solana_clock_refresh_interval = 10`.  10 seconds for now.
2. Fixed the Rebalancer freezing bug! Root cause was blocking async Solana RPC client API, apparently it is trying to spin off another async call in current thread that is already blocked by waiting for it to complete! Deadlock at it's bestest! :-) Creating and using dedicated Tokio runtime with few threads solved the issue. 
3. Finally decoupled the liquidator's main() method from Tokio runtime. Instead the liquidator is now creating runtime instances with smaller thread pool sizes that are  incapsulated in processes that are using third party async API. This helps to better manage rather insane number of Tokio threads.

## Overview
This PR enhances the status icon capabilities with dynamic management and adds a comprehensive menu system. With these changes, status icons can now be created dynamically (without needing to edit dashboard YAML), and an optional menu system allows users to toggle display of additional status icons for navigation and actions.

## Key Features

### Status Icons Enhancement
- **Dynamic Creation**: Status icons can now be programmatically added/removed via service calls
- **Flexible Format**: New `type:target|icon|label` format for defining icon behavior
- **Action Types**: Support for view navigation, entity control, and service calls
- **Timeouts**: Optional automatic removal after specified time period
- **Proper Layout**: Menu button (when enabled) always appears at end of status bar

### New Menu System
- **Optional Feature**: Completely opt-in from
- **Toggle Function**: Show/hide menu items with service call or menu button
- **Dynamic Items**: Menu items use same format as status icons
- **Context Awareness**: Auto-filters current view from menu options
- **Auto-Timeout**: Configurable auto-close timeout

### Implementation
- **Menu Manager**: New component that handles menu state, toggles, and timeouts
- **Template System**: Three new dynamic templates for generating icons:
  - `dynamic_view_item`: For navigation actions
  - `dynamic_entity_item`: For entity toggle controls
  - `dynamic_service_item`: For service calls
- **Helper Functions**: New normalization and processing functions

## New Services

### `toggle_menu`
Show or hide the menu for a View Assist entity.
```yaml
service: view_assist.toggle_menu
data:
  entity_id: sensor.view_assist_living_room
  show: true  # optional, defaults to true
  timeout: 15  # optional, overrides configured timeout temporarily
```

### `add_status_item`
Add one or more items to the status bar or menu.
```yaml
service: view_assist.add_status_item
data:
  entity_id: sensor.view_assist_living_room
  status_item: "view:weather|weather-sunny"  # or list of items
  menu: false  # false = status bar, true = menu items
  timeout: 30  # optional, auto-remove after timeout
```

### `remove_status_item`
Remove one or more items from the status bar or menu.
```yaml
service: view_assist.remove_status_item
data:
  entity_id: sensor.view_assist_living_room
  status_item: "view:weather|weather-sunny"  # or list of items
  from_menu_items: false  # false = status bar, true = menu items
```

## Configuration Options
- **enable_menu**: Turn on/off menu functionality
- **menu_items**: List of items to show when menu is active
- **enable_menu_timeout**: Auto-close menu after timeout
- **menu_timeout**: Time in seconds before menu auto-closes
- **show_menu_button**: Show permanent menu button in status bar

## Status Icons vs Menu Icons

### Similarities
- Both use the same dynamic icon templates
- Both follow the same format: `type:target|icon|label`
- Both support the same action types (view, entity, service)
- Both can be programmatically managed through services
- Both can have timeouts for automatic removal of individual items

### Differences
- **Visibility**: Status icons are always visible; menu icons only appear when menu toggled
- **Behavior**: Menu automatically filters current view items; status bar shows all configured items
- **Interaction**: Menu items replace status icons when active, then revert when deactivated

## Dynamic Status Icon Format
The format `type:target|icon|label` is used for both status and menu items:

- **Type**: The action type - "view", "entity", or "service"
- **Target**: Path, entity_id, or service to act on
- **Icon**: Icon name without mdi: prefix (optional, defaults based on type)
- **Label**: Optional

Examples:
```
view:weather|weather-sunny|Weather
entity:light.kitchen|lightbulb|Kitchen
service:script.goodnight|moon|Goodnight
```

## Breaking Changes
None - all functionality is backward compatible with existing configurations.

## Notes
- Legacy status icons (added in dashboard YAML) continue to work
- Configuration referencing templates by name (e.g., "weather") still works
- Requires changes to the dashboard.yaml found [here](https://github.com/dinki/View-Assist/pull/161)

body: ## Enhance delete_path endpoint with two-step confirmation ### Summary This PR improves the security of the /delete_path endpoint by introducing a two-step delete confirmation process using ephemeral confirmation tokens. My main goal here @tjbck was to ensure that hallucinations or runaway LLMs don't inadvertently go blowing away parts of a user's filesystem. ### Major Changes - ✳️ Introduced a two-step confirmation mechanism for file/directory deletion: - First request returns a confirmation token and expiry timestamp. - Second request (with token) confirms and executes deletion. - New response model: ConfirmationRequiredResponse. - Updated DeletePathRequest model to replace confirm_delete with confirmation_token. - Persistence logic: - Pending confirmation tokens are stored in .pending_confirmations.json. - Expired or mismatched requests are safely rejected. - Token expires after 60 seconds. ### Additional Improvements - 🔄 Moved ALLOWED_DIRECTORIES config into a new config.py file. - 🧼 Removed unused print/debug statements. - ⚙️ Minor imports and dependency updates for clarity (e.g. uuid, json, Union). ### Version Bumped API version from 0.1.0 → 0.1.1. --- ✅ Safe for review and merge.
